event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: A meticulous review of the 2024-02-28 SBAC filing shows no direct or even indirect discussion of the COVID-19 pandemic or any pandemic-driven disruptions. None of the enumerated risk factors mention health crises, epidemics, global supply-chain shocks caused by lockdowns, labor shortages attributable to illness, prolonged remote-work transitions, or any sustained shift in consumer wireless demand tied to COVID-19. The company does reference other hazards—natural disasters, remote-work cyber-risks, and macro-economic factors such as inflation—but these are not attributed to, or framed around, the pandemic event. Consequently, under the Time Decay Principle (the pandemic is now almost four years old and would warrant only moderate scoring if evidence existed), the complete absence of pandemic-specific language means there is no scorable evidence at all. The overall risk signal for COVID-19 in this document is therefore assessed as non-existent, resulting in a net severity score of 0.
